record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.context_brief: Even-degree split Jacobian loci in M_2
record.original_question: Let C be a genus-2 curve over C whose Jacobian is (n,n)-isogenous to a product E_1 x E_2 of elliptic curves, and let L_n be the corresponding locus in the moduli space M_2 of genus-2 curves. For the even degrees n=4 and n=6, determine the loci L_4 and L_6 in M_2 and determine the relation between the elliptic curves E_1 and E_2 in each case.

evidence.quote: For our purposes, Ln will simply be the locus of genus 2 curves whose Jacobian is (n, n)-isogenous to a product of two elliptic curves.
Problem 3. Determine the loci Ln in M2 for n = 4, 6. Further, determine the relation between the elliptic curves E1 and E2 in each case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{M}_2$ denote the coarse moduli space of smooth projective curves of genus $2$ over $\mathbb{C}$. For a positive integer $n\ge 2$, define the locus
$$L_n \;=\; \{\,[C]\in\mathcal{M}_2 \;:\; \text{the Jacobian } \mathrm{Jac}(C) \text{ admits an } (n,n)\text{-isogeny to a product } E_1\times E_2 \text{ of elliptic curves}\,\},$$
where an $(n,n)$-isogeny $\mathrm{Jac}(C)\to E_1\times E_2$ is an isogeny of principally polarized abelian surfaces whose kernel is isomorphic to $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^2$ and is isotropic for the Weil pairing on $\mathrm{Jac}(C)[n]$.

Carry out the following for the even degrees $n=4$ and $n=6$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Determine the locus $L_n\subset \mathcal{M}_2$ explicitly, i.e.\ describe it as an algebraic subvariety of $\mathcal{M}_2$ (for instance, by explicit equations in the Igusa invariants $J_2,J_4,J_6,J_{10}$ of genus-$2$ curves).
\item For a generic point $[C]\in L_n$, determine the relation between the two elliptic factors $E_1$ and $E_2$ (e.g.\ describe their $j$-invariants as a correspondence, identify any isogeny between them, etc.).
\end{enumerate}
artifact.status_search_result: The loci $L_n$ have been explicitly described for $n=2$ (classical, and Shaska–Völklein), $n=3$ (Shaska), and $n=5$ (Shaska and collaborators). The literature notes that the cases $n>3$ are substantially harder, and explicit descriptions of $L_4$ and $L_6$ together with the relation between the two elliptic factors do not appear to have been published; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Genus two curves covering elliptic curves: a computational approach
status_evidence.snippet: The space L_2 was studied in Shaska/Völklein and the space L_n for n=3,5 was studied by Shaska where an algebraic description was given as a sublocus of M_2.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit algebraic descriptions of L_n have been obtained for n=2,3,5 but not for n=4,6.

status_evidence.title: Isogenous components of Jacobian surfaces (Beshaj–Elezi–Shaska)
status_evidence.snippet: Cases when n>3 are more difficult; Frey and Kani note the difficulty of producing explicit examples.
status_evidence.claim: Cases n>3, including n=4,6, are documented as substantially harder and not yet treated explicitly.
